instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Consequences Compound
cards.instruction: Make each new choice carry a larger reward, cost, audience, or point of no return.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed below you. Our table-tennis game decides who cleans up tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I signed for a borrowed bat. That's the equipment book.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, putting commitments in writing. Loser cleans for the whole month; enter that beside the bats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm returning mine at six, when the club meets. I haven't agreed to your bet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll settle the terms at six in front of the club. If you agree there, everyone gets to hold us to the month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I copied your big label for our nut biscuits. Pick the best ones; your name's on the plate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My label says NUTS, not my name. It warns people with allergies.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, information first. Write your name under it so the committee knows whose judgment to trust.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put the plate by the door, then. People can see the warning before taking one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your chair there too. Everyone who tries one can tell you personally what they think.

cards.title: Make Help Define Us
cards.instruction: Get their help, then use how it is offered to redefine what the relationship means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drew a line through the sentence like you. Help me make this complaint sound firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My line means delete it. You crossed out the only sentence saying what went wrong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, drawing attention to it. Put it back and help me sharpen it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fix the wording, but only your name goes on the complaint. I can't risk my job over this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're my editor, not my spokesperson. Leave the anger in; I'll sign for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm lifting this end the way you did. Take the other end; let's move the table together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only lifted it to check the loose leg. It will fall off if we carry it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, checking together. Help me tighten it. I'm tired of being the friend you do everything for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold the leg straight. You turn the screw until it grips.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep holding. Next time you introduce us, try 'we fix things together' instead of 'I look after him.'

cards.title: Reopen the First Reason
cards.instruction: Keep them present by returning to the first reason for staying and revealing that it now means something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm blowing on mine like you. Stay until the tea's cool, at least.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was blowing a tea leaf off the rim. Yours has been cold for ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the rim. Then stay until we've finished drinking it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can sit for five minutes, but I don't want any more tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the five minutes without tea. It's the two of us sitting together I don't want to finish.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my key beside yours. Don't go until we've checked the return properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm returning yours because I've moved out. You don't need to hand your own key back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, comparing them. Stay while we make sure this one still opens the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll test it once, then leave it on the table for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Test it from the outside. I'd like to see you use it to come in once more before you leave it behind.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I accept your apology for missing my concert. I bowed when the conductor bent down; you would have liked the finish.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He was picking up his baton. You bowed to your music stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, acknowledging everyone. Now apologize for leaving me to do that without one friendly face watching.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. I watched the recording last night, straight after the concert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say you're sorry for keeping that to yourself. I spent all evening thinking nobody I knew had seen the end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for admitting you broke the vase. I pointed at the dog just as firmly as you did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was pointing him away from the glass, not saying he broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, keeping him clear. Now apologize for letting me spend three days calling him destructive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. I'll take him for a long walk to make it up to him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me you should have corrected me before you take him. He gets the walk; I need that sentence.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can my aunt and uncle come for tea? I've put folded towels in the bath like yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tea's fine. My towels are there because the shower leaks, not for guests.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, keeping them handy. Aunt and Uncle can use the towels when they stay tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said tea. The only working shower is in my room, and I want an early night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain your shower times while they're having tea. They'll need to wash before you go to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can I put an extra chair in the hall, beside the one you put out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Mine's out there because the paint's wet. Don't sit on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, reserved seating. Mine will be for the chair of our new tenants' committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a committee. I only said you could leave a chair there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need to choose the committee first. Stay beside your wet chair and count the votes; you won't have to sit down.
